title: First-component extraction in linear time
statement: There are a finite Turing machine $M$ and a constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, on every Boolean input $x$, $M$ halts within $c(|x|+1)$ steps and outputs the first component parsed from $x$ by the aligned pair parser, or the empty word if parsing fails.
replaced:
There exist a finite Turing machine $M$ and a constant $c$ such that $M$
computes, within $c\,(n+1)$ steps on inputs of length $n$, the function
sending a word in the self-delimiting pair code to the first component of the
encoded pair, and any malformed word to the empty word.
